title.narrative: Urban Water Resilience: Providing WASH Services in Time of Severe Crisis

description.narrative:
**Long-term impact Water (WASH)**
Better performance of urban water and sanitation local corporation in times of crisis and health hazards by enhanced safe coverage of water and sewerage services, improved recovery of costs and systematic emergency preparedness – contributing to improved public health and water delivery for a population of 8 million people
​
**Medium-term impact**
- Partnerships between persons and organisations are inclusive and sustainable Cooperation between (high and low performing) urban water and sanitation local corporations in Yemen and WEC consolidated under the aegis of the Yemen Water Partnership/MetaMeta
​
- Organisations key to (sectoral) inclusive development of partner countries are strengthened by inflow of enhanced workforce Fifteen Urban Water and Sanitation Local Corporations able to effectively deliver safe water and sanitation services in spite of the constraints of the war situation by capacitating concerned staff
​
- Water network better managed in 5 out of 15 Urban Water and Sanitation Local Corporations
​
- Sewerage facilities better managed in 5 out of 15 Urban Water and Sanitation Local Corporations

description.narrative:
In this section (maximum 1000 words), please
**For TMT+:**
Comment to what extent the outputs have been achieved. Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
The main achievements of the project at the moment of the formal ending date are as follows: 1- A total of 96 persons have been trained directly in the training and 16 Resilience and Service Improvement Plans (RSIP) have been developed clearly showing the huge challenges water utilities face in the very difficult situation in Yemen. However a larger number of people is being reached as participants in the training had to work on concrete assignments which required dialogue with other staff in their organization. The training also is already benefitting students at WEC as their teachers use the material developed in the training and the lessons learned, in their regular training program. So we are confident that the number of people that will be reached through different training channels of WEC will further increase as envisaged in the project proposal.
2- The project involved working with a total of 32 organizations and with seven of them an MoU was signed with WEC: Faculty of Engineering, faculty of Agriculture, Bena Foundation, Banan Foundation, Dhamar University, Aden University and The General Authority to Protect the Old cities.
3- A resilience case study was developed by WEC staff together with MetaMeta of the Ibb water utility to gain more familiarity with the situation on the ground. The study shows the complexity of the situation but also how Ibb was able to cope with some problems.
4- A Training of Trainers (ToT) training for WEC was implemented in April 2020 in Sana’a Yemen. It meant to be in Amman but because of Covid-19 the location was adjusted and the training approach was changed to a combination of class room and on-line training. WEC staff was trained on several topics including utility efficiency, cost recovery, service resilience, emergency preparedness, water safety planning from source to tap and back, gender mainstreaming in water supply, solar power for water supply, lessons from the experience of Ibb water utility, water utility simulation game and on an annotated outline of a resilience assessment and plan. After the ToT the course material including presentations, training material, exercises, and tools were developed by WEC staff and MetaMeta.
5- A National Competition for Good Practice in Service Provision by water utilities during Severe Crisis was launched to obtain access to relevant information and experience that could benefit the training. This turned out being a successful approach as we received 15 applications with 117 documented practices including both practices that are being applied as well as ideas that were not yet implemented. Most relevant practices were all published in Arabic on the website. In addition a selection was made of a total of 18 practices that were published in a booklet in English and shared in Yemen and abroad. A national event was held to i) announce the winners of the award; ii) present the training approach and the need to focus on resilience and service improvement and iii) present the booklet. This event was held on Sana’a in WEC with the participation of 8 teams from Sana’a Water and Sewerage Local Corporation, 6 other LCs (from within Yemen) and the a team from the National Water Sewerage Authority (NWSA) besides several high level participants.
6- A template was developed for the Resilience and Service Improvement Plan (RSIP). This was done by WEC staff and MetaMeta working together with 3 staff members from Sana’a water utility who participated in the ToT. The staff from Sana’a water utility used the template to develop their draft RSIP s. The trainees developed the plan and presented it to the management and staff of Sana’a water utility. We got very encouraging feedback. The utility used the developed plan in its 2021 annual plan and for its strategic policies and interventions. Based on this experience the format of the RSIP was fine tuned.
7- Three training batches were implemented each consisting of three events in WEC (two of three days and one of two days) with assignments under the guidance of coaches in between events. In each batch teams from five utilities participated reinforced by a participant from NGO’s. The first training event prepared trainees for problem analysis with results being presented in the second training event in WEC. Trainees received comments on their presentation which allowed them to make improvements and received training on possible solutions. With this information they implemented their second assignment to prioritize their problems and identify possible solutions. In the third training event at WEC the draft resilience plans were presented and thereafter adjusted on the basis of comments received under guidance of the coaches. Final results than was send to WEC and presented to the management of each utility.

title.narrative: I.S.1. Number of beneficiaries in the society reached with knowledge, skills and techniques

comment.narrative: 20-07-2022: This figure is derived from the Resilience and Service Improvement Plans as submitted by the LCs (available at www.resiliencewater.com). It includes total city population and % served IDPs (internally displaced people) the corresponding subtotals are 7,026,495 (population) and 944,421 (IDPs). Noting that city population may not reflect all the people actually being served. An overview of total subscribers can also be found in the RSIPs and in attached file.

In the development of training curriculum of WEC, we targeted the largest utility in terms of population served (Sana’a) with a population of 3.2 million people. A resilience plan is already drafted and used for the utility 2021 plan.
Next group will contain 5 utilities with a served population of 1.7 million. Next one will target another 5 utilities with 1.6 million people.
After the project end, WEC alone will target third and forth batches (10 smaller utilities) with a population of 1.0 million people
Then will be a regular module for WEC targeting other staff of the utilities and NGOs and other urban and rural service providers
So beneficiaries are 6.5 million by the end of the project and 7.5 million one year after the project.
